project.name: tokenledger
project.purpose: An auditable token-usage ledger for AI agents, built on enterprise internal-control principles: vouchers, authorization, reconciliation, and a tamper-evident audit trail. Each token-consuming event becomes an append-only voucher; spending is compared against pre-issued authorization vouchers; the ledger can be reconciled against a provider bill.
implemented: Append-only voucher ledger in JSONL, with a SHA-256 hash chain linking each voucher to its predecessor.
Gapless sequential voucher numbering (TL-YYYY-NNNNNN for usage, TA-YYYY-NNNNNN for authorization).
SQLite index used only as a derived cache; the JSONL ledger is the single source of truth and the index can be rebuilt at any time.

Authorization vouchers define a scope (agent, project, model), a period, and a limit in currency or tokens. Usage is compared against them at booking time. Over-limit vouchers are still booked, but flagged.
Pricing is deliberately empty by default: the tool refuses to guess vendor prices. Unpriced usage is marked 'unpriced' and can never be silently treated as zero cost.
Idempotent ingestion via deduplication keys, so re-reading the same log does not double-book.
Log parser for the Codex CLI rollout format, plus a generic JSONL parser with configurable field mapping.
Commands: init, record, ingest, query, report, budget, reconcile, verify, reindex, export, history.
Exit codes for automation: 3 audit failed, 4 reconciliation mismatch, 5 budget exceeded.
verified: 22 unit tests pass (standard library unittest only).
Ingested 296 vouchers from 9 real Codex CLI session logs covering 13.8 million tokens; the hash chain audit passed.
Session-level reconciliation passes: the sum of per-turn deltas equals the cumulative total reported in the source logs.
constraints: Python 3.11 or newer, standard library only, zero runtime dependencies.
Must run unchanged on Windows, macOS and Linux; no hard-coded paths.
Local-first: no cloud service, no data leaves the machine.
Append-only by design: there is no update or delete command; corrections must be new reversing entries.
known_limitations: The hash chain proves a booked voucher was not altered after booking, but it cannot prove the source agent log was not altered before ingestion.
Only the Codex CLI log format is parsed out of the box; other agents need a small new parser or manual field mapping.
All documentation is in Chinese, including the README and the internal-control mapping document.
Model prices must be filled in by hand before any currency-based limit can be evaluated.
No user authentication or multi-user access control; it assumes a single trusted operator.
project.user_context: A single developer on Windows who uses the Codex CLI daily, wants internal-control-grade accounting for AI token spending, and intends to release the project as open source.

agent_parsers.title: Add parsers for other AI coding agents
agent_parsers.what: Write log parsers for additional agents (for example Claude Code, Gemini CLI) so one ledger covers every agent the user runs, instead of only the Codex CLI.
agent_parsers.effort: Medium. Each parser is a small module plus tests; the ingestion, pricing, authorization and audit layers already work for any source.
agent_parsers.risk: The log formats are undocumented and change between versions, so parsers can break silently and under-report spending.

english_readme.title: Translate and expand the documentation into English
english_readme.what: Provide an English README, an English internal-control mapping document, and a short architecture note, so an international audience can evaluate and adopt the tool.
english_readme.effort: Low to medium. Writing only; no new code paths.
english_readme.risk: Documentation can drift from the code if it is not exercised by tests.

log_signing.title: Add cryptographic attestation of source agent logs
log_signing.what: Make pre-ingestion tampering detectable, for example by having the agent or a wrapper sign each log segment with an HMAC or key pair, and having the ledger store and verify that signature at ingestion time.
log_signing.effort: High. Requires a signing wrapper around the agent, key management, a verification step in the parser, and a policy for unsigned historical logs.
log_signing.risk: Adds operational complexity for every user, and most existing logs would remain unsigned.

Judged only by how much the candidate improves this tool's fitness for its stated purpose, which single next step should be built next?

criteria.agent_parsers: Add parsers for other AI coding agents so one ledger covers every agent the user runs, not only the Codex CLI.
criteria.english_readme: Translate and expand the documentation into English so an international audience can evaluate and adopt the tool.
criteria.log_signing: Add cryptographic attestation of source agent logs so pre-ingestion tampering becomes detectable, not only post-booking tampering.
criteria.none_of_these: None of the three is the right next step; something else in `project` matters more right now.

readiness.instructions: Based on `project`, how ready is this tool to be used for real, financial-grade control over AI token spending by a small team, as opposed to being a personal prototype? The lowest level is 0 and the highest is 4.
criteria: Prototype: works on one machine and one agent, offers no protection against pre-ingestion tampering, documentation in a single language.
Useful to its author for personal cost tracking, but clear gaps block team use.
Usable by a small team that standardises on the same agent tooling, with accepted manual setup and manual price entry.
Usable by a team with mixed agent tooling and provides evidence strong enough for an internal review.
Suitable for external audit or regulated use without further assurance work.

chinese_only_docs_acceptable.instructions: For a project whose stated goal is to be usable by others as open source, is Chinese-only documentation an acceptable state to leave in place for now?

criteria.true: Chinese-only documentation is acceptable for the current stage; it does not block the stated goal yet.
criteria.false: Chinese-only documentation materially blocks adoption by the intended audience and should be addressed.

log_signing_required.instructions: For this tool to be credible as internal control over spending rather than a convenience report, is cryptographic attestation of source logs (evidence that a log was not altered before ingestion) a requirement rather than a nice-to-have?

criteria.true: A requirement: without it, the evidence chain has a gap that an auditor or a sceptical reviewer would reject.
criteria.false: A nice-to-have: the post-booking hash chain and reconciliation already provide enough assurance for this use case.
